Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "can you clean this up into a clear prompt for drafting a practical lighting handoff for our thursday rehearsal? use the notes as the source, keep the conditions and both branches, and leave the quotes as they are. please organize the request but don't make the handoff itself

REFERENCE NOTES BEGIN
The Alder Room is a  ninety-seat theatre in the back of the old Mercer Library. Its lighting crew for Thursday's rehearsal is Nia Bell, the board operator, Tomas Reed, the electrician, and Elio Park, who is covering the follow spot for the first time. The stage manager, June Vale, expects the company at 18:15 and has asked the crew to be ready for a cue-to-cue at 18:30. The room has a fixed ladder that can reach the first electric, but the rolling ladder is needed for the side boom. The lighting desk is an ETC Ion, and the crew's marked-up channel sheet is in a blue folder on the prompt desk.

At 14:40 Nia found that the dimmer relay for circuit 17, which feeds the upstage-left practical, clicked twice after a blackout. The practical is a shaded table lamp used in the opening scene; it is not a work light. Tomas isolated circuit 17, tagged the breaker, and wrote the time on the electrical log. The lamp itself worked when he tested it on a portable dimmer, so the crew has not treated the bulb as the source of the fault. They have not yet run a sustained test on the relay. Nia told June, “The lamp is fine on the portable; I don't want to call the circuit safe until Tomas has watched it under load.”

Tomas plans to inspect the relay after the afternoon class leaves the room. He will first check the terminal connections with the circuit isolated, then restore power for a brief test while Nia watches the desk readout. If the relay holds steady for ten minutes by 16:30 and Tomas records that result in the electrical log, Nia may repatch the practical to circuit 17 and use its existing cue levels for Thursday's rehearsal. If the relay clicks again, the readout fluctuates, or Tomas cannot complete the test by 16:30, do not repatch the practical to circuit 17; leave the breaker isolated and use the spare LED practical on circuit 9 instead. Circuit 9 is already patched as channel 29, but its warm setting needs to be checked against the tablecloth.

The spare LED practical belongs on the same table, about a hand's width behind the book stack, with its cable taped along the rear leg. Elio measured the position during Tuesday's spacing rehearsal and marked the tabletop with a small piece of removable blue tape. June asked that the mark stay until the opening-scene check is complete, because the actor playing Mara puts down a cup beside the lamp and has caught the cable once before. The lamp's inline switch should face the prompt side so the actor can reach it without crossing the playing area. The source does not need to be hidden from the audience; the shade should simply face downstage as it does in the existing blocking.

Nia has saved the current show file as “Alder Thu 0411” and made a separate copy named “Alder Thu 0411 test.” She wants the crew to work in the test copy during the circuit check, then return to the show file before the company arrives. The lighting plot uses channel 29 for the spare practical and channel 17 for the original practical; those channel numbers must not be confused with the breaker number. Tomas has a paper copy of the plot with the cable route marked in pencil. The folder also contains a cue list from the previous Thursday, but June said it reflects an earlier version of the opening and should be used only to confirm cue names, not levels.

At 15:10 Elio checked the follow spot from the rear platform. The lamp came up cleanly, but the iris handle stuck briefly when it was nearly closed. He cleaned the track with the approved cloth, tried the handle three times, and wrote “slight drag near closed” beside the spot note on the channel sheet. He did not force the handle or remove the iris assembly. Nia asked him to leave the follow spot at half intensity until the cue-to-cue so June can decide whether the opening needs a tighter pickup. The gel frame is a pale straw, not the amber frame listed on the older cue sheet, and the spare pale-straw frame is in the labeled drawer under the booth counter.

1. Before the company enters, Nia should confirm which practical is in use by checking Tomas's electrical log and the patch in the Ion test copy. If the circuit 17 test meets the ten-minute condition and is logged by 16:30, the original practical can be restored to its existing cue levels; otherwise, circuit 17 stays isolated and the crew uses the LED practical on circuit 9, channel 29. In either case, Nia should verify that the lamp responds to its recorded cue and that the table position and cable route match the stage mark. June should be told which practical is in use before the opening-scene check.

2. Tomas is responsible for removing the isolation tag only if he has completed and recorded the required circuit 17 test; Nia should not remove it on his behalf. If the LED practical is used, Tomas should leave the circuit 17 breaker isolated and make a note that the alternate is in service. The spare lamp's warm setting must be compared with the tablecloth under the rehearsal look, because the portable test in the afternoon does not settle that visual check. Elio can help hold the shade in position, but he is not assigned electrical work. The crew can make that comparison during the opening-scene check without delaying the rest of the cue-to-cue.

3. At 18:30, June will call the opening sequence once with the actor playing Mara and once without the actor, so Nia can check the table practical and Elio can check the follow-spot pickup. Elio should keep the spot at half intensity until June has seen the first pass; after that, he should change it only if June gives him a level or pickup adjustment. If the iris still drags near closed, Elio should report it to Nia and leave the handle where it moves freely rather than forcing it. June's note from Tuesday says, “Let the face arrive before the table goes bright,” but she has not supplied a new cue number or level, so the handoff should not assign either one.

The crew has a short access window because a library reading ends at 14:20 and the building manager locks the rear loading door at 22:00. The rolling ladder must be returned to the marked alcove before the audience entrance route is reopened, while the fixed ladder can remain at the first electric until the crew finishes focusing. Nia will keep the Ion's test copy available through the cue check, then confirm the active file name with June before saving any approved changes to the show file. The crew should record the final practical choice and any unresolved iris drag in the prompt-desk log, where Friday's operator can find it without relying on a verbal handoff.

At the end of rehearsal, after June releases the crew, Tomas will check whether circuit 17 was returned to service or remained isolated and make sure the electrical log matches the breaker tag. If the circuit 17 relay passed the earlier test and the original practical was used, Nia should restore the show file's existing channel 17 levels and tell Tomas before he closes the log. If the LED practical was used instead, the crew should leave circuit 17 isolated, keep the channel 29 patch in the show file only if June has confirmed that arrangement for the next call, and note that confirmation is still pending if she has not. Elio should return the pale-straw spare frame to its labeled drawer, and the blue folder should go back to the prompt desk.
REFERENCE NOTES END", "output": "Organize the request below into a clear prompt for drafting a practical lighting handoff for the Alder Room crew before Thursday's rehearsal. Keep the circuit 17 decision and both conditional branches intact, including their conditions and the later instructions that depend on which practical is used.
